To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the present generation DSP TMS320C67x can be used to design real time wavefront processors, that the performance of such a system scales with the number of actu- ators, and that the principal bottleneck is the memory bandwidth.

(1) The performance of a Shack Hartmann natural AO system is limited by the available memory bandwidth and the IPC bandwidth of the processors; (2) The compute latency scales as the number of actuato rs, the number of DMs, the number of guide stars and the number of pixels read out by the camera; and (3) A 10x increase in compute latency will require 10x increase of the memory bandwidth of the processor.

(a) the compute latency of a single DM natural guide star system is dominated by memory bandwidth, (b) the compute latency scales as the square root of the number of actuactors, and (c) the memory bandwidth of the processor is the most critical factor in determining the performance of an adaptive optics system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and analysis of real time wavefront processors that will enable the next generation of AO systems.
the development of a real-time wavefront control system for the next generation adaptive optics (AO) telescopes.
how the performance of a real-time wavefront processor will scale as the number of actuactors increase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present generation of DSPs is adequate for a 104 increase, but not for a 105 or 106 increase, in actuator utilization.
the present generation processors are not adequate for the next generation AO systems.
the present generation of DSPs is capable of supporting a single DM AO system with 1000 actuators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the performance of the present generation DSPs are not sufficient for future AO systems.
the performance of an adaptive optics system is limited by the available memory bandwidth and IPC bandwidth of the processors.
the present generation DSP processors are capable of supporting a large scale AO system with up to 104 actuators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
future AO systems that use a single processor will be limited by the available memory bandwidth and that the performance of such systems will not scale with the number of DMs.

the compute latency of a wavefront processor can be predicted with reasonable accuracy, and the performance of the wavefront processor can then be used to predict the performance of the entire AO system.

the compute latency of a Shack Hartmann AO system can be reduced by an order of magnitude with the use of today's DSP processors, and that a further order of magnitude improvement is possible with the introduction of future DSP processors that are capable of higher memory bandwidth and IPC bandwidth.
